title: Intraline emphasis carried by a rule (BPR-0323)
reference_disclaimer: One accept-or-reject, and a different kind of answer from the last two. Both previous batches offered points on one axis — how strong a tint — and you rejected the axis twice, for two different and correct reasons. This is not another tint. The mark is a rule under the characters, which does not depend on a fill being able to differ from its row, so it behaves the same on a washed row as an unwashed one and in a high-contrast profile as a standard one. If the rule is the wrong instrument, say so and the next batch can show an outline or a bold weight instead; the mechanism is in place and swapping the mark is cheap now.

subjects.display_name: Changed characters are marked with a rule, not only a tint
subjects.description: Both of your last notes said a tint could not carry this. A tint keeps its own hue, so it read as red on a blue row; and in the high-contrast profiles the row fills already sit at the ends of the range, so a tint had nowhere to travel and those profiles showed the least contrast of any. So the mark is now a rule under the changed characters, drawn in the code's own text colour, in every profile and on every row. The accepted fills stay exactly where they still work: an unselected row in any profile keeps the salmon and green you chose. A selected row drops them for a deeper shade of the band it is actually wearing, so nothing foreign sits inside the blue.
acceptance_criteria: Changed characters are findable in every profile
High-contrast Dark is at least as emphatic as the standard profiles, not less
On a selected row nothing reads as a foreign colour inside the band
Unselected rows keep the fills accepted in the earlier batch
The rule does not disturb the alignment of the monospaced code
known_concerns: The rule is drawn in `syntax_normal`. That is the one colour the existing contrast audit already guarantees is legible on every background the diff can paint, so the rule inherits that guarantee rather than needing a threshold of its own.

A selected row's fill is derived from that row's own washed band and holds its hue to within a degree, at a separation of 9.0 — much lower than an unselected mark's 20.0, because the rule is carrying the mark there and spending more would cost text contrast the band already spent.
Offscreen QFusionStyle at device pixel ratio 1; not native macOS artwork.
The moved-row case from your first note is still not shown, because it cannot occur: a moved row can never carry an intraline mark.

audit_verdict.note: Rendered through the real UIforETW course in all four profiles, every capture emitting UIFORETW_SELECTED_DIFF_EVIDENCE_OK. Tests assert the rule and the derived fill and fail without them.

media_groups.title: The two states that failed before
media_groups.note: Light: the top row is selected — check nothing red or green sits inside the blue band. High-contrast Dark: check the marks are now the most visible rather than the least.

items.label: Light — selected row at the top

detail_sections.heading: What changed
items: A rule is drawn under every changed run, in every profile, on selected and unselected rows alike.
Unselected rows keep the accepted C3 fills unchanged.
Selected rows take a fill derived from their own washed band instead of a palette colour, so the hue matches the band.
Nothing about the row bands, the selection wash, the connectors, or the navigation icons changed.
